## Abstract {.unnumbered}

Repeating or rescaling existing stock characteristics can change a tuned investment rule without adding information. On a common U.S. stock panel, selective replication and theme balancing alter economic attribution and stock holdings across four portfolio methods. Payoff responses depend on the method, costs, and missing-return valuation. Stock-ridge controls isolate the induced penalty change. Actual expansion from 39 to 153 characteristics has small, uncertain predictive effects under the evaluated procedures. A simulation shows that test prediction can improve without new information. Library updates therefore require separate assessment of represented inputs, estimated exposures, and cost-dependent payoffs.

*Keywords:* stock characteristics; feature redundancy; portfolio choice; return prediction; regularization; model attribution. *JEL classification:* G11, G17, C52, C58.

## Interactive figures (in preparation)

Three interactive figures are in preparation. Each will be built from the paper's results package and carry a caption naming the manuscript figure or table it reproduces:

- **Theme multiplicity.** Column counts and correlation participation ranks for the 13 Jensen–Kelly–Pedersen themes, with the monthly participation rank of a selected theme.
- **Omitting a theme.** The change in loss when one theme is left out of the library, with pointwise and simultaneous intervals, and how the portfolio composition moves across methods, cost scenarios and blocks.
- **Cost sensitivity.** Mean annual return and Sharpe ratio of the four portfolio methods and three representations across one-way costs from 0 to 100 basis points.

Until they are published, every result is in the [paper (PDF)](/assets/pdfs/Characteristic_Libraries_and_Portfolio_Decisions_SSRN_v2.pdf).
